project_requirements.title: What the call wants
project_requirements.question: What must the project address, develop and achieve?

cards.title: Central object
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop?
cards.answer:
Low-voltage direct-current (LVDC) microgrids in city buildings or neighbourhoods, with design tools, a real-life demonstration and support for regulation and standards.
An LVDC microgrid connects the DC devices in a building (solar panels, batteries, LED lighting, IT equipment, heat pumps, EV chargers) on a local direct-current network, linked to the normal alternating-current (AC) distribution grid through one central converter. The call expects it to save energy and materials, optimise storage and self-consumption, support grid stability and allow islanded operation.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–161 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-01, Scope

cards.title: Scope
cards.question: Which activities fall within the funding opportunity's scope?
cards.answer:
Proposals are expected to address all seven aspects the call lists; the call names no excluded activities.
- Develop safe, sustainable LVDC design methods and tools, including grid monitoring, control and safe handling of DC faults at affordable cost, and assess life-cycle costs and benefits against AC installations, including impacts on the AC distribution grid (harmonics, ancillary services, demand response) and on vulnerable consumers' bills
- Demonstrate in real life an LVDC microgrid connecting all electrical applications in at least one residential, office or commercial building or one neighbourhood; the proposal must already review local regulations and grid codes and show the demonstration is possible, if needed through pre-agreed regulatory relaxation or an innovation sandbox
- Demonstrate LVDC virtually, by digital twin simulation, in other buildings, including at least one under renovation, in different cities and countries and, if possible, a vulnerable urban area; at least 3 real and virtual demonstrations in total
- Identify regulatory barriers at European, national and distribution system operator level, and propose solutions
- Contribute to standardisation in CEN-CENELEC and IEC (the European and international standards bodies), notably with use cases
- Develop awareness, education and training materials for authorities, the public, students, planners, developers and installers, with local academia
- Disseminate results, engage stakeholders from the planning phase, and organise at least one open workshop with site visits
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–161 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-01, Scope

cards.title: Problem
cards.question: What type of problem or need must justify the project, and where must it originate?
cards.answer:
Most building devices run on DC, but buildings are wired for AC, causing conversion losses and heavier connections to city grids.
The need originates with cities and society: European Green Deal, Clean Industrial Deal and Solar Strategy goals, energy efficiency, local renewables and resilience. The call notes that an LVDC microgrid needs a much smaller connection to the AC distribution grid than a traditional installation, reducing pressure on city grids. Barriers are mainly awareness, acceptance, safety concerns, regulation and standards.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–161 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-01, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: Deliverables
cards.question: Which concrete outputs must the project produce?
cards.answer:
Design tools and methods, a real-life LVDC demonstration, virtual demonstrations, regulatory recommendations, standardisation input and training materials.
- LVDC design methods and tools, and a life-cycle cost-benefit methodology
- At least one real-life LVDC microgrid, and enough virtual demonstrations to reach at least 3 in total
- Technical installation guidelines and recommendations on regulatory alignment for authorities and distribution operators
- Use cases and other contributions to CEN-CENELEC and IEC standards
- Awareness, education and training materials
- At least one open workshop with site visits
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–161 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-01, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: Impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer:
Projects must contribute to all four outcomes: awareness, measurable acceptance, uptake in cities through guidelines, and more regulatory options and standards for LVDC.
- Improved awareness of LVDC microgrids' potential for the Green Deal, Clean Industrial Deal, SET Plan and Solar Strategy
- Increased acceptance, with significant and measurable contributions to safety (especially DC faults), energy and resource efficiency, renewable and storage integration, demand response, peak shaving and resilience, and where applicable proof that LVDC lets energy communities share assets
- Increased uptake in cities through technical guidelines and regulatory recommendations to authorities and distribution operators
- More regulatory options and standards supporting EU industry leadership in LVDC
The call requires measurable contributions but sets no numerical targets.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–161 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-01, Expected Outcome

cards.title: After the project
cards.question: How must the result be replicated, taken up and kept in use after the project?
cards.answer:
The results must enable wider uptake: guidelines, regulatory proposals and standards are mandatory, and the project joins the Cities Mission's clustering.
- Transferability: virtual demonstrations in different cities and countries must assess regulatory feasibility and costs and benefits elsewhere
- Standards: contribution to CEN-CENELEC and IEC is required
- Knowledge: training and education materials, dissemination and an open workshop
- Network: a Memorandum of Understanding with the Cities Mission Platform (the support platform of the EU Mission for 100 climate-neutral cities) as soon as possible after the start, and clustering with other Cities Mission projects; cooperation with the other projects under this topic
The call does not say who must operate the demonstration after the project.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–161 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-01, Specific conditions and Scope

cards.title: Number of partners
cards.question: What is the permitted or required consortium size?
cards.answer:
At least three independent organisations from three different countries; the call sets no maximum.
The general rule requires, as beneficiaries (organisations that sign the grant agreement and receive funding), three legal entities independent of each other: at least one established in an EU Member State and two others each in a different Member State or country associated with Horizon Europe (non-EU countries taking part in the programme, such as Norway, Switzerland or the United Kingdom). Affiliated entities (organisations legally linked to a beneficiary) and associated partners (organisations taking part without funding) do not count towards this minimum.
In addition, at least three cities from three different Member States or Associated Countries must be beneficiaries, represented by a local authority or an entity with its explicit consent; at least one must be one of the 112 cities of the EU Mission on Climate-Neutral and Smart Cities.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 13 · B — Eligibility, Consortium composition
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–161 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-01

cards.title: Partner composition
cards.question: Which types of partners must the consortium include?
cards.answer:
At least three cities must be beneficiaries, one of them a Mission city, and social sciences and humanities experts are required.
- Cities: three, from three different Member States or Associated Countries, each represented by a local authority or an entity with its explicit consent; at least one of the 112 Mission cities
- Social sciences and humanities: contributions from these disciplines and involvement of SSH experts and institutions are required, especially for training and stakeholder engagement
- Local academia and research partners: for education and training materials
- Exclusion: entities controlled by China or a Chinese legal entity are not eligible
Proposals should build on earlier projects, notably Shift2DC, HYPERRIDE, TIGON, HYNET and THEUS.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–161 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-01, Specific conditions and Scope

cards.title: Distribution of work
cards.question: How must work and budget be distributed among partners?
cards.answer:
The call prescribes no budget split, but the work plan must include resources for cooperation with the Cities Mission Platform and for clustering.
Since the grant is a lump sum (a fixed amount paid against completed work packages), the consortium must allocate the amount to work packages and partners in a detailed budget table.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–161 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-01, Specific conditions and Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents, lump sum grant proposals

cards.title: Coordinator
cards.question: What type of organisation may or must act as lead applicant?
cards.answer:
No type of organisation is prescribed: the beneficiaries choose one of themselves as coordinator.
The coordinator manages and coordinates the project and represents the consortium towards the granting authority (the European Commission or its agency). At submission it must confirm that it has the mandate to act for all applicants.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Coordinator
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents, Submission

project_requirements.title: TenneT's position
project_requirements.question: What is TenneT's position within the consortium?

cards.title: Coordinate
cards.question: Can TenneT apply or coordinate, and under which conditions?
cards.answer:
Formally yes, but the project is about building-level DC networks in cities, so TenneT TSO B.V. would not be a natural lead.
Any eligible beneficiary may coordinate, and a Dutch entity is eligible. TenneT does not count towards the three required cities.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 11, 36 · B — Entities eligible for funding; IMPORTANT, Coordinator
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–161 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-01, Specific conditions

cards.title: Participate
cards.question: Can TenneT take part without receiving funding?
cards.answer:
Yes, as an associated partner, which takes part without funding and bears its own costs.
An associated partner does not sign the grant agreement, cannot charge costs, does not need legal validation and does not count towards the minimum of three beneficiaries from three countries. It must still register in the Participant Register before the application is submitted.
TenneT could, for example, advise on how LVDC microgrids and their ancillary services affect the wider grid.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 5 · B — Eligibility, Associated partners
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Registration, Consortium roles and Associated partners
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–161 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-01

cards.title: Receive funding
cards.question: Can TenneT receive funding, and which funding rate or cost rules apply?
cards.answer:
Yes: as a beneficiary TenneT can receive up to 70% of its eligible costs, paid within a lump sum.
This topic is an innovation action (a project that develops, pilots and demonstrates new or improved solutions close to the market), for which the maximum rate is 70% for organisations other than non-profit legal entities. The grant is a lump sum fixed from a detailed budget and paid against completed work packages. The expected EU contribution is around EUR 7 million per project, for the whole consortium. The call sets no Dutch national rules.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · G — Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–161 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-01, Specific conditions

cards.title: TenneT's likely contribution
cards.question: What contribution would make TenneT credible and useful within the project?
cards.answer:
TenneT's possible contribution is limited to the system view: how LVDC microgrids' lower connection needs and ancillary services could ease congestion.
This is our interpretation. The life-cycle assessment must include impacts on the overall energy system, such as demand response and ancillary services, and the call stresses reduced pressure on city grids. TenneT could provide congestion data from Dutch regions, input from the regional Energy boards, and flexibility requirements from its balancing work. The microgrids themselves sit behind the connection of distribution grids, so Dutch DSOs are the more natural grid partners.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–161 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-01, Scope

project_requirements.title: Innovation
project_requirements.question: What type of innovation must the project develop?

cards.title: Innovation threshold
cards.question: Must the project produce genuinely new knowledge or technology, or may it integrate and apply existing solutions?
cards.answer: The project must develop innovative design methods and tools and demonstrate LVDC in real life; it builds on earlier projects such as Shift2DC.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–161 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-01, Scope

cards.title: Innovation object
cards.question: In what must the project innovate?
cards.answer: A combination of technology (LVDC design, control and fault protection), regulation and standards, and social aspects such as acceptance and training.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–161 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-01, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: Development stages
cards.question: Which development stages must the project cover?
cards.answer: Design and tool development, real-life and virtual demonstration, and preparation for wider uptake through guidelines and standards.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–161 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-01, Scope

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?
cards.answer:
Activities are expected to reach TRL 7–8 by the end of the project.
TRL 7 is a system prototype demonstrated in an operational environment; TRL 8 is a complete and qualified system.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–161 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-01, Specific conditions, Technology Readiness Level
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 15 · B — Technology Readiness Levels

project_requirements.title: Work
project_requirements.question: Which activities or work structure must the project cover?

cards.title: Demonstration
cards.question: Where and under which conditions must the solution be demonstrated?
cards.answer:
At least one real-life LVDC microgrid connecting all electrical applications in a building or neighbourhood, plus virtual demonstrations to reach at least 3.
Virtual demonstrations use digital twins (numerical models of buildings) in other building types, including one under renovation, in different cities and countries. The real demonstration must be shown to be legally possible in the local context already at proposal stage.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–161 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-01, Scope

cards.title: Integration
cards.question: How must the activities fit together and with existing systems?
cards.answer:
The microgrid must integrate all electrical applications of the building and connect to the AC distribution grid through a central converter.
The assessment must cover the impact on the AC grid, such as harmonics and support through ancillary services, and the project must cluster with other Cities Mission projects such as those on positive energy district digital twins.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–161 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-01, Scope

cards.title: Evidence
cards.question: What must the demonstration prove?
cards.answer:
The project must produce measurable evidence on safety, efficiency, integration, demand response, peak shaving and resilience, and life-cycle costs and benefits.
Costs and benefits must be assessed technically, environmentally, economically and socially, including the effect on vulnerable consumers' energy bills, and compared with traditional AC installations.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–161 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-01, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: User participation
cards.question: How must users take part in the project?
cards.answer:
Residents, users, industry and researchers must be engaged from the planning phase, with at least one open workshop and site visits.
Social sciences and humanities experts must help make the work relevant to society.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–161 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-01, Scope

cards.title: Safety and cybersecurity
cards.question: Which safety, cybersecurity or data requirements must the project meet?
cards.answer:
Safe handling of DC faults is a core requirement; the call sets no cybersecurity rule.
- Safety: design tools must ensure safe handling of DC faults; acceptance must show measurable contributions to human and building safety
- Control restriction: entities controlled by China or a Chinese legal entity are not eligible
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–161 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-01, Specific conditions, Expected Outcome and Scope

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
About 3 projects of around EUR 7 million each are expected, within a topic budget of EUR 20 million.
- Total project size: not stated
- Grant request: around EUR 7 million per project, for the whole consortium; other amounts may be requested and selected
- Funding form: lump sum (a fixed amount set from a detailed budget and paid against completed work packages)
Final budgets may change by up to 20% after evaluation.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 27–28 · Call HORIZON-MISS-2027-04, Overview of this call
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–161 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-01, Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 29 · F — Budget flexibility

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
Companies such as TenneT receive at most 70% of eligible costs; non-profit legal entities receive up to 100%.
- For-profit organisations: up to 70% of eligible costs, so at least 30% must come from their own resources
- Non-profit legal entities (for example universities and research organisations): up to 100% of eligible costs
- Co-financing conditions: the call sets no rule on cash or in-kind co-financing beyond the funding rate; the remainder is simply not reimbursed
Grants may not produce a profit: any surplus of revenue plus grant over costs is deducted from the final grant.
For lump sum grants the rate is applied when the lump sum is calculated and does not appear in the grant agreement.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · G — Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount

cards.title: Budget constraints
cards.answer:
The grant is a lump sum fixed from a detailed budget table, which must still follow the normal cost-eligibility rules.
- Eligible costs: the detailed budget table must contain only costs that would be eligible under an actual-cost grant (personnel, subcontracting, purchases, other direct costs), because the lump sum must approximate the costs actually incurred
- Overheads and VAT: indirect costs are included in the lump sum calculation at the standard 25% flat rate of direct costs (excluding subcontracting)
- Subcontracting or equipment: purchases and subcontracting must give best value for money and be free of conflicts of interest; ineligible costs in the budget table can lead to a reduced grant, even late in the project
Payment depends on completing the work packages, not on proving the costs.
- Mandatory allocations: the work plan must include activities and resources for cooperation with the Cities Mission Platform and clustering
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents, lump sum grant proposals
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 32 · G — Budget categories and cost eligibility rules

cards.title: Cash flow and financial exposure
cards.answer:
Partners normally receive a large advance after signing, minus a 5–8% contribution to a shared insurance fund, then interim payments.
- Payment model: pre-financing (an advance) of normally 160% of the average EU funding per reporting period, then interim payments linked to periodic reports, and a final payment after the final report fixes the grant
- Retention or guarantee: 5% to 8% of the maximum grant is deducted from the pre-financing and paid into the mutual insurance mechanism (a fund covering sums that cannot be recovered from beneficiaries)
- Financial reporting or audit: depending on grant size and type of beneficiary, a certificate on the financial statements may be required; each beneficiary is liable only for its own debts
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 32–33 · G — Reporting & payment arrangements, Certificates, Liability regime for recoveries

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
One stage: full proposals are due by 7 October 2027, 17:00 Brussels time, through the EU Funding & Tenders Portal.
- Stage 1 — Full proposal: 7 October 2027, 17:00 Brussels time; Part A online and Part B of at most 45 pages (the limit for lump sum innovation actions), with a detailed lump sum budget table and a review of local regulations and grid codes for the demonstration
- Opening: 9 February 2027
- Additional procedure: none; the Commission may open the call up to one month earlier or later and delay the deadline by up to two months
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 27–28 · Call HORIZON-MISS-2027-04, Overview of this call
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–161 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-01, Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 3–4 · A — Admissibility, Page limits

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
The call sets no duration or start date: both are fixed in the grant agreement.
- Maximum duration: not set by the call; the grant agreement states the duration in months, and extensions are possible only exceptionally
- Required start: normally after the grant agreement is signed; an earlier start is possible only exceptionally, for duly justified reasons and with the granting authority's agreement
- Conditions after the start: the Memorandum of Understanding with the Cities Mission Platform must be concluded as soon as possible after the starting date
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 30–31 · G — Starting date & project duration

cards.title: Decision and contracting
cards.answer:
Indicatively, the evaluation result comes about 5 months after the deadline and the grant agreement is signed about 8 months after it.
- Funding decision: about 5 months after the deadline (indicative), around March 2028
- Grant agreement: about 8 months after the deadline (indicative)
- Conditions before starting: an invitation to grant preparation is not yet a funding commitment, since legal entity validation, financial capacity and exclusion checks follow; the partners must sign a written consortium agreement
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 30 · F — Indicative timetable for evaluation and for signature of the grant agreement
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 29 · F — No commitment to provide funding
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Consortium agreement

funding_timing_submission.title: Application
funding_timing_submission.question: Mandatory information to include in the application

cards.title: Mandatory submission package — pass/fail
cards.answer:
The proposal must be complete, submitted electronically before the deadline, and within the page limit; incomplete applications are rejected.
- Application form: Part A (administrative data and a summary budget, filled in online) and Part B (the technical description, uploaded as a PDF) through the EU Funding & Tenders Portal, using the forms inside the submission system; Part B is limited to 45 pages
- Budget: the summary budget in Part A and a detailed budget table, which is the basis for the lump sum
- Mandatory annexes: a plan for the exploitation and dissemination of results, including communication activities, and the ethics self-assessment
- Partner documents: the coordinator confirms at submission that it has the mandate to act for all applicants; every participant signs a declaration of honour before the grant is signed
- Registration: every beneficiary, affiliated entity and associated partner needs a participant identification code (PIC, a number from the EU Participant Register) before submission; validation of beneficiaries follows at grant preparation
- Parallel submission: none
- Lump sum: the detailed budget table is mandatory and is used to fix the lump sum
- City consent: cities not represented by their local authority need its explicit consent
- Regulatory review: the proposal must include a review of local regulations and grid codes showing the real-life demonstration is possible
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 3–4 · A — Admissibility, Page limits
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 5 · B — Entities eligible to participate
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 15 · B — Ethics
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Registration
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–161 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-01, Specific conditions and Scope

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
cards.answer:
Independent experts score three criteria out of 5; a proposal needs 3 on each and 10 in total, and Impact weighs 1.5 times in the ranking.
- Evaluation criteria: Excellence (clear, ambitious objectives beyond the state of the art; sound methodology), Impact (credible pathways to the expected outcomes; dissemination and exploitation measures) and Quality and efficiency of the implementation (work plan, risks, resources, capacity of each partner)
- Thresholds: at least 3 out of 5 for each criterion and 10 out of 15 overall
- Weighting: for ranking, the Impact score counts 1.5 times
- Ranking rules: equal scores are separated first by whether a proposal covers aspects of the call not covered by higher-ranked ones, then by the Impact score, then Excellence, then gender balance among lead researchers and geographical diversity
- Budget assessment: the grant awarded may be lower than requested, and topic budgets may change by up to 20% after evaluation
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 23–26 · D — Award criteria, Scores and weighting, Two-stage calls
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 28–29 · F — Evaluation procedure and ranking, Budget flexibility
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 31 · G — Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount

cards.title: Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
Three city beneficiaries including a Mission city, the Cities Mission Platform agreement, the lump sum and the China-control restriction are specific to this topic.
- Conditional — cities: three cities from three countries as beneficiaries, one of the 112 Mission cities
- Conditional — Cities Mission Platform: a Memorandum of Understanding soon after the start, with resources for cooperation and clustering; grants are linked to the platform's action HORIZON-MISS-2021-CIT-02-03
- Conditional — social sciences and humanities: SSH experts and institutions must be involved
- Exception — regulation: the demonstration may rely on pre-agreed regulatory relaxation or an innovation sandbox
- Exception — entities controlled by China: not eligible
- Recommended: build on Shift2DC, HYPERRIDE, TIGON, HYNET and THEUS; cooperate with the other projects of this topic
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 157–161 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-01, Specific conditions and Scope
